body:
Hi Dan,

This is most probably happening at this line: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/native/fsevents.cc#L132 

However it is unclear why this is happening. Can you tell me more about the circumstances of the failure? 605134 seems like a large number of paths for a single poll. Were their a large number of files changed at once?
We don't have a reliable repro case for this, but perhaps knowing that it has to do with a large number of paths for a single poll, that can help us repro the bug.
Ok I will wait for more info. Thanks for reporting it!
How often does it poll? Does the server poll in the background even if I'm not executing Bazel commands, or does it wait to drain the poll until a build starts?
Apparently only on command. This would explain why the number of change is so important.
It seems like it would be prudent to use a thread to drain the queue from time to time.
/cc @haxorz: how often the WatchService is pulled? It seems like we are overflowing the watch queue.

I find this is fairly easy to reproduce by
1. having a directory with a lot of files (npm 2 is particularly good at making `node_modules` dirs like this)
2. running bazel build on a target in that package
3. simultaneously running `rm -r node_modules`
I have a pending fix, just need to repro to make sure we actually do fix the problem

Unfortunately I cannot reproduce with a simple example. @znull: if you have a workspace in which you can reproduce this behavior, please send it to me.

I'll send out my patch whatever happens and hopefully this will address this issue.

Here's a semi-reliable repro. https://github.com/dfabulich/watch-repro

The `WORKSPACE` is empty, and the `BUILD` file is a single target:

``` python
genrule(
    name='x',
    srcs=glob(['data/*.txt']),
    outs=['x.txt'],
    cmd='echo hello > $@',
)
```

`repro.sh` is a bash script:

``` bash
#!/bin/sh
mkdir -p data
DATE=`date`
for I in {1..100000}; do
    echo $I $DATE > data/$I.txt
done
bazel build :x & rm -rf data
```

When I run `./repro.sh` I have about a 75% chance of reproing this AIOOBE on OS X El Capitan 10.11.6
